title: Haralambis' equality conjecture for three-element distance sets
statement:
Let $D$ be a three-element set of non-negative integers. Let $\kappa(D)$ be the supremum, over real $t$, of the smallest distance from $td$ to an integer as $d$ ranges over $D$, and let $\mu(D)$ be the supremum of the densities of sequences whose pairwise differences do not lie in $D$.

**Haralambis' equality conjecture.** Every three-element $D$-set satisfies

$$
\kappa(D)=\mu(D).
$$

The conjecture is presented in the conclusion as a particularly interesting problem because exact computation of $\mu(D)$ is difficult in general. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
source_name: Daphne Der-Fen Liu and Grant Robinson, “Sequences of Integers with Three Missing Separations”, arXiv:1611.03940 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.03940

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2016). “The conjecture has been proved true for $|D| \leq 6$ (cf. ), and remains open for $|D| \geq 7$.”

title: Davila–Kenter's lower-bound conjecture for the zero forcing number
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with girth $g\ge 3$ and minimum degree $\delta\ge 2$. Its zero forcing number $Z(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a zero forcing set, where a zero forcing set is a set of initially black vertices from which the color-change rule eventually colors every vertex black.

**Davila–Kenter's conjecture.**

$$
Z(G) \ge \delta + (\delta - 2)(g - 3).
$$

This conjecture gives a readily computable lower bound for the zero forcing number, a graph invariant introduced in connection with minimum-rank problems for matrices associated with graphs. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Randy Davila, Thomas Kalinowski and Sudeep Stephen, “A lower bound on the zero forcing number”, arXiv:1611.06557 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.06557

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

title: Aharoni–Zerbib's generalization of Tuza's conjecture
statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph. For a positive integer $m$, let $\nu^{(m)}(H)$ be the maximum size of a collection of edges no two of which share $m$ or more vertices, and let $\tau^{(m)}(H)$ be the minimum size of a collection of $m$-sets such that every edge of $H$ contains one of them.

**Aharoni–Zerbib's generalization of Tuza's conjecture.** Every $3$-uniform hypergraph satisfies

$$
\tau^{(2)}(H)\leq 2\nu^{(2)}(H).
$$

This extends the triangle-hypergraph formulation of Tuza's conjecture to all $3$-uniform hypergraphs. The source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Ron Aharoni and Shira Zerbib, “A generalization of Tuza's conjecture”, arXiv:1611.07497 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07497

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

title: Asymptotic optimal pebbling conjecture for eight-wide staircase graphs
statement:
Let $S_{8,n}$ be the eight-wide staircase graph, and let $\pi_{\operatorname{opt}}(G)$ be its optimal pebbling number, the minimum size of a solvable pebbling distribution on $G$.

**Eight-wide staircase conjecture.**

$$
\pi_{\operatorname{opt}}(S_{8,n})=\frac{5}{4}n+O(1).
$$

The paper obtains the value for $S_{8,8}$ by computer search but notes that even the $n=9$ case is computationally difficult. The conjecture predicts the asymptotically optimal growth rate for the eight-wide family.
source_name: Ervin Győri, Gyula Y. Katona, László F. Papp and Casey Tompkins, “The Optimal Pebbling Number of Staircase Graphs”, arXiv:1611.09686 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.09686

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

title: Polynomial degree conjecture for secant varieties of Gaussian moment varieties
statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{n,d}$ be the Gaussian moment variety of order $d$ in $n$ variables, and let $\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathcal{G}_{n,d})$ denote its $k$-th secant variety. Fix $k$ and $n$, and consider the degree of this secant variety as a function of the moment order $d$. **Polynomial degree conjecture.** For fixed $k$ and $n$, the function

$$
d\longmapsto\deg\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathcal{G}_{n,d})
$$

is a polynomial in $d$, starting from the smallest value of $d$ for which the secant variety does not fill the ambient space. The preceding discussion emphasizes that even determining defining ideals can be difficult, so this conjecture concerns a more accessible numerical invariant; its general validity remains open.
source_name: Carlos Améndola, Kristian Ranestad and Bernd Sturmfels, “Algebraic Identifiability of Gaussian Mixtures”, arXiv:1612.01129 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01129

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Palindromicity conjecture for hyperplane sections of high-degree complete intersections
statement: Let $P=\mathbb{P}^N$, and let $X\subset P$ be a general complete intersection of multi-degree $(d_1,d_2,\ldots,d_k)$ with $d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_k$. Assume that $d_1\gg0$. For a hyperplane $H\in P^{\vee}$, write $Y:=X\cap H$. **Palindromicity conjecture.** The hyperplane section $Y$ is palindromic. This conjecture generalizes the preceding result for hyperplane sections of general cubic $4$-folds, and asks whether palindromicity persists for hyperplane sections of general complete intersections when the smallest defining degree is sufficiently large.
source_name: Patrick Brosnan, “Perverse obstructions to flat regular compactifications”, arXiv:1612.01220 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01220

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Maximum-transversal conjecture for order-four latin hypercubes
statement: Let $Q^n(\mathbb{Z}_4)$ and $Q^n(\mathbb{Z}_2^2)$ denote the $n$-dimensional latin hypercubes isotopic to the Cayley tables of the corresponding iterated groups. A **transversal** is a set of $4$ entries containing all distinct symbols and lying pairwise at Hamming distance $n$. **Maximum-transversal conjecture.** Among all latin hypercubes of order $4$, the maximum number of transversals is attained by the odd-dimensional Cayley tables of the iterated group $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and by the Cayley tables of the iterated group $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$. The paper establishes exact counts for these group-derived hypercubes and characterizes the order-four hypercubes with no transversals, but the asserted global maximality remains conjectural.
source_name: Anna Taranenko, “Transversals in completely reducible multiary quasigroups and in multiary quasigroups of order 4”, arXiv:1612.01797 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Uniform condition-number conjecture for the trace Schur complement
statement:
Let $\lambda_{\min}(s,h)$ and $\lambda_{\max}(s,h)$ be respectively the smallest and largest generalized eigenvalues of the trace Schur-complement matrix relative to the fractional norm matrix ${\mathsf{H}}_s$, with $s<0$. Define the condition number by

$$
\kappa(s,h)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(s,h)}{\lambda_{\min}(s,h)}.
$$

**Uniform condition-number conjecture.** There exist $s<0$ and a constant $C$ such that

$$
\kappa(s,h)\leq C\qquad\forall h>0.
$$

This weaker requirement asks only for a mesh-independent condition number, rather than uniform lower and upper spectral-equivalence bounds; the source presents it as an additional computational criterion.
source_name: Miroslav Kuchta, Kent-Andre Mardal and Mikael Mortensen, “Preconditioning trace coupled 3d-1d systems using fractional Laplacian”, arXiv:1612.03574 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.03574

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Gruslys–Leader–Tomon generalized bounded-remainder poset-packing conjecture
statement:
Let $P$ be a poset. A **partition into copies of $P$ with remainder** is a collection of pairwise disjoint copies of $P$ in the Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$, together with the elements not covered by those copies.

**Gruslys–Leader–Tomon conjecture.** The Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$ can be partitioned into copies of $P$ and a remainder of at most $c=c(P)$ elements.

This generalization drops the requirement that $P$ have a minimum and a maximum. The source says that proving it would resolve the earlier Gruslys–Leader–Tomon conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
source_name: Vytautas Gruslys and Shoham Letzter, “Almost partitioning the hypercube into copies of a graph”, arXiv:1612.04603 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.04603

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2016). “This conjecture was recently proved by Tomon .”

title: Bump-Friedberg generating-function identity for covering groups
statement:
Let $(\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)},\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_R^{(n)})$ be a fundamental pair with $n\mid(\mathbf{p}\cdot n_\alpha)$. Let $\Theta(\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_R^{(n)},\chi)$ be the distinguished theta representation whose associated character satisfies $\nu_R=\mathbf{1}$, and let $\mathcal{W}^{\operatorname{GL}_R}_{\mathcal{O}_0}$ be its unique Whittaker model. Let $\widetilde{\Delta}_s$ be the anti-genuine, $K_r$-biinvariant function on $\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)}$ specified by the stated torus support and value. **Bump-Friedberg identity.** For every $\widetilde{g}\in\widetilde{\operatorname{GL}}_r^{(n)}$,

$$
\int_{U_r}\widetilde{\Delta}_{n_\alpha s-\frac{R-1}{2}}(u\widetilde{g})\psi(u)\,du=|\det(\widetilde{g})|^{s-\frac{R-r}{2}}\overline{\mathcal{W}^{\operatorname{GL}_R}_{\mathcal{O}_0}}(\phi(\widetilde{g})).
$$

This identity is presented in the supplied text as a consequence of the generating-function approach of Bump and Friedberg to the Bump-Hoffstein conjecture; no resolution evidence is supplied.
source_name: Fan Gao, “Generalized Bump-Hoffstein conjecture for coverings of the general linear groups”, arXiv:1612.04879 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.04879

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Threshold conjecture for universality in bounded-degree graphs
statement:
For an integer $\Delta\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{H}(n,\Delta)$ denote the class of graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and say that a graph is $\mathcal{H}(n,\Delta)$-universal if it contains every graph in this class. **Universality threshold conjecture.** A threshold function for the property that $G(n,p)$ is $\mathcal{H}(n,\Delta)$-universal is 
$$
p\sim\left(n^{-1}\log^{1/\Delta}n\right)^{\frac{2}{\Delta+1}}.
$$
 This is the threshold for the appearance of $K_{\Delta+1}$-factors; the conjecture asserts that the threshold for one such factor is also the threshold for the simultaneous appearance of every graph in $\mathcal{H}(n,\Delta)$.
source_name: Asaf Ferber, Gal Kronenberg and Kyle Luh, “Optimal Threshold for a Random Graph to be 2-Universal”, arXiv:1612.06026 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.06026

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: The odd-configuration inversion conjecture
statement:
Let $n=2m+1$, and let $\widetilde{\Delta^n}$ denote the stable configurations reachable from $\Delta^n$ by chip-firing. In the odd case, these configurations may be identified with permutations, and an inversion is a pair of entries in the permutation that occur in reverse order. **Odd-configuration inversion conjecture.** The maximum number of inversions among all permutations in $\widetilde{\Delta^n}$ is exactly

$$
m.
$$

The conjecture concerns the structure of reachable stable configurations for odd $n$. It had been verified in the source for odd $n\leq9$, but no general proof was given.
source_name: Sam Hopkins, Thomas McConville and James Propp, “Sorting via chip-firing”, arXiv:1612.06816 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.06816

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Fox–Lee–Sudakov lower bound for topological cliques
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $\sigma(G)$ be the largest integer $t$ such that $G$ contains a subdivision $TK_t$.

**Fox–Lee–Sudakov conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\chi(G)=k$ satisfies

$$
\sigma(G)\ge c\sqrt{k\log k}.
$$

The conjecture gives a quantitative lower bound on the size of a topological clique in terms of chromatic number. The supplied source gives no evidence of resolution, so it remains open.
source_name: Dawei He, Yan Wang and Xingxing Yu, “The Kelmans-Seymour conjecture IV: a proof”, arXiv:1612.07189 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Edge-cover conjecture for the intersection of two matroids
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal Q$ be matroids on the same ground set. For a simplicial complex $\mathcal C$, let $\beta(\mathcal C)$ denote the minimum number of members of $\mathcal C$ whose union covers the ground set. **Edge-cover conjecture.**

$$
\beta(\mathcal P\cap\mathcal Q)\le \max\bigl(\beta(\mathcal P),\beta(\mathcal Q)\bigr)+1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the possible extra cost of intersecting two matroids in an edge cover. The paper notes that it is sharp if true, gives a factor-two upper bound, and reports a proof in the case $\beta(\mathcal P)=\beta(\mathcal Q)=2$; no complete resolution is supplied here.
source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Dani Kotlar and Ran Ziv, “Fair representation in the intersection of two matroids”, arXiv:1612.07652 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07652

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Milans–Stolee–West conjecture on unbounded track number of line graphs
statement:
Let $(G_n)_{n=1}^{}$ be a sequence of graphs. Write $\chi(G)$ for the chromatic number of $G$, $L(G)$ for its line graph, and $\tau(G)$ for the minimum number of interval graphs whose union is $G$. **Milans–Stolee–West conjecture.** If

$$
\chi(G_n) \mathrel{\longrightarrow} \infty,
$$

then

$$
\tau(L(G_n)) \mathrel{\longrightarrow} \infty.
$$

This conjecture asks whether unbounded chromatic number forces unbounded track number for line graphs; the source paper proves it, together with asymptotically stronger lower bounds for complete graphs, so the conjecture is resolved.
source_name: Deepak Rajendraprasad, “Track number of line graphs”, arXiv:1612.08347 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08347

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2016); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Conjecture on the circular separation dimension of planar graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $\pi^\circ(G)$ denote its circular separation dimension, the minimum number of circular orderings of the vertices of $G$ needed to separate every pair of non-adjacent edges.

**Planar circular separation dimension conjecture.** The circular separation dimension of $G$ is at most two:

$$
\pi^\circ(G)\leq 2.
$$

For planar graphs, the known upper bound is $3$, while $\pi^\circ(G)=1$ exactly for outerplanar graphs. Thus the conjecture concerns whether every planar graph that is not outerplanar admits two circular orderings separating all non-adjacent edges.
source_name: Arpitha P. Bharathi, Minati De and Abhiruk Lahiri, “Circular Separation Dimension of a Subclass of Planar Graphs”, arXiv:1612.09436 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09436

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

title: Three-node equivalence conjecture for persistent path and Dowker homology
statement:
Let $(X,A_X)$ be a three-node dissimilarity network. Write 1-dimensional persistent path homology for the persistent homology produced by persistent path homology (PPH), and write 1-dimensional Dowker persistent homology for the corresponding Dowker construction.

**Three-node equivalence conjecture.** On three-node networks, 1-dimensional PPH is isomorphic to 1-dimensional Dowker persistent homology.

This conjecture proposes that the two persistence methods agree in dimension one on the smallest nontrivial asymmetric networks. It is based on experimental observations; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond the conjecture.
source_name: Samir Chowdhury and Facundo Mémoli, “Persistent Path Homology of Directed Networks”, arXiv:1701.00565 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.00565

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: Binary-alphabet extremal conjecture for abelian-square factors
statement: For a finite word, an **abelian-square factor** is a factor formed by concatenating two anagrams of one another. Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $k$ be the number of distinct abelian-square factors in a word of length $n$. **Binary-alphabet extremal conjecture.** If a word of length $n$ contains $k$ distinct abelian-square factors, then there exists a binary word of length $n$ containing at least $k$ distinct abelian-square factors. This conjecture asserts that binary words attain the maximum possible number of distinct abelian-square factors among words of each fixed length; the source leaves it as an open question.
source_name: Gabriele Fici, Filippo Mignosi and Jeffrey Shallit, “Abelian-Square-Rich Words”, arXiv:1701.00948 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.00948

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2017). “This conjecture was later confirmed, and the smallest possible size of an alphabet for which it holds is known to be $4$ .”

title: Conjecture on transfers of test functions
statement:
Let $E \geq F' \geq F$ be a tower of number fields, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $F$ containing the infinite places, and let $S'$ and $S_0$ be the places of $F'$ and $E$ above $S$. Let $\Pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_E)$, and suppose $\Pi^{\sigma}\cong\Pi$ for every $\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(E/F)$. A transfer is a triple of compactly supported smooth functions $f_{S_0}$, $h_{S'}$, and $\Phi_S$ satisfying the trace identity of Definition of the paper for every irreducible generic unitary representation $\pi_S$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S)$; a function is of positive type in the sense used there. **Transfer conjecture.** There exist $f_{S_0}\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(E_{S_0}))$ and $h_{S'}\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(F'_{S'}))$ admitting a transfer $\Phi_S\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S))$ of positive type such that the transfer identity holds for every irreducible generic unitary representation $\pi_S$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F_S)$ and

$$
\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{S_0})(f_{S_0})\neq 0.
$$

The conjecture asserts that sufficiently many transfers can detect every Galois-invariant cuspidal representation; the paper notes that it is known in some special settings, including $n=2$ and cyclic extensions of prime degree, but remains open in general.
source_name: Jayce R. Getz, “An approach to nonsolvable base change and descent”, arXiv:1701.01766 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01766

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: Sum-Balaban extremal dumbbell-like graph conjecture
statement:
Let $D_{a,b,a'}$ be a dumbbell graph, and assume $a\leq a'$. A **dumbbell-like graph** $D_{a,b,a'}^{\ell}$ is obtained from $D_{a,b,a'}$ by inserting $\ell$ edges between $v_1$ and $K_a$ when $\ell>0$, or removing $-\ell$ edges between $v_{b-1}$ and $K'_{a'}$ when $\ell<0$.

**Dumbbell-like graph conjecture.** Dumbbell-like graphs $D_{a,b,a'}^{\ell}$ attain the minimum value of sum-Balaban index.

The conjecture is supported by the paper's computer experiments, which examine dumbbell and dumbbell-like graphs for a range of orders. The supplied status evidence identifies it as an open problem.
source_name: Martin Knor, Jaka Kranjc, Riste Škrekovski and Aleksandra Tepeh, “On the minimum value of sum-Balaban index”, arXiv:1701.02716 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.02716

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “For further recent topics and open problems in chemical graph theory an interested reader is referred to .”

title: Kreutzer–Oum–Seymour–van der Zypen–Wood conjecture on majority 3-colourings of digraphs
statement: Let $D$ be a digraph. A colouring of $D$ is **$\frac{1}{2}$-majority** if every vertex has the same colour as at most half of its out-neighbours. **Kreutzer–Oum–Seymour–van der Zypen–Wood conjecture.** Every digraph is $\frac{1}{2}$-majority $3$-colourable. This is the unresolved case $k=2$ of the problem of determining the smallest number $m(k)$ such that every digraph is $\frac{1}{k}$-majority $m(k)$-colourable; a $4$-colouring is known, while the conjectured bound of $3$ remains open.
source_name: António Girão, Teeradej Kittipassorn and Kamil Popielarz, “Generalised Majority Colourings of Digraphs”, arXiv:1701.03780 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.03780

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “Surprisingly, this is open even for $k=2$. Kreutzer, Oum, Seymour, van der Zypen and Wood gave an elegant argument showing that every digraph is $\frac{1}{2}$-majority $4$-colourable and they conjectured that $m(2)=3$.”

title: The maximum principle conjecture for the Riesz transform
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative finite Borel measure with compact support and continuous density with respect to the Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $0<s<d$. The $s$-Riesz transform (potential) of $\mu$ is

$$
R^s\mu(x)=\int\frac{y-x}{|y-x|^{s+1}}\,d\mu(y).
$$

**Maximum principle conjecture.** There is a constant $C=C(d,s)$ such that

$$
\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}|R^s\mu(x)|\le C\sup_{x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu}|R^s\mu(x)|.
$$

This relation was known for $d-1\le s<d$ and is proved in the paper for $0<s<1$ and for radial measures, while it remains open in the general case. The conjecture is stated for nonnegative measures; it is false for non-positive measures.
source_name: Vladimir Eiderman and Fedor Nazarov, “On the maximum principle for the Riesz transform”, arXiv:1701.04500 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: Equal-separation converse conjecture for planar point sets
statement:
Let $X$ be a set of $N$ points, let $K$ be the number of parts in an equal separation, and let $d(Y)$ denote the minimum degree of a curve through a subset $Y\subseteq X$. **Equal-separation converse conjecture.** If $X$ cannot be separated equally, then

$$
\max\limits_{Y\subseteq X}\frac{|Y|}{K\cdot d(Y)}\gg\frac{N}{K^2}.
$$

This conjecture would make low degree the only obstruction to equal separation, strengthening the best known necessary criterion discussed in the paper. Its status is open.
source_name: Nikhil Marda, “On Equal Point Separation by Planar Cell Decompositions”, arXiv:1701.04529 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04529

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “Together, these open problems and conjectures leave many paths for building on results from this paper.”

title: Colour-critical graph Ramsey extremal conjecture
statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. A graph $H$ is **colour-critical** if there exists an edge $e\in E(H)$ such that $\chi(H-e)<\chi(H)$. Let $\mathrm{ex}^r(n;H,\ldots,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph that is not $(H,r)$-Ramsey, and let $t_k(n)$ denote the number of edges in the Turán graph with $k$ parts. **Colour-critical extremal conjecture.** Whenever $n$ is sufficiently large,

$$
\mathrm{ex}^r(n;H,\ldots,H)=t_{R_\chi(H,\ldots,H)-1}(n).
$$
This would generalise the cited theorem for colour-critical graphs and establish tightness of the corresponding extremal inequality. The supplied material does not establish whether the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Robert Hancock, Katherine Staden and Andrew Treglown, “Independent sets in hypergraphs and Ramsey properties of graphs and the integers”, arXiv:1701.04754 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04754

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: The hemisphere volume conjecture for metric balls
statement:
Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$, let $B(p,R)$ be a metric ball, and let $inj(M)$ denote the injectivity radius. A hemisphere of intrinsic radius $R$ is a ball of radius $R$ in the sphere of constant curvature $(\frac{\pi}{2R})^2$. Let $\alpha(n)$ denote the volume of the unit $n$-sphere. **Hemisphere volume conjecture.** If

$$
R \leq \frac{1}{2}inj(M),
$$

then

$$
Vol(B(p,R))\geq \frac{\alpha(n)}{2}\left(\frac{2R}{\pi}\right)^n.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $B(p,R)$ is isometric to a hemisphere of intrinsic radius $R$. Hemispheres are conjectured to have the smallest volume among metric balls of fixed dimension and radius; nonsharp lower bounds are known in all dimensions, but the sharp conjecture remains open even in dimension two.
source_name: Gregory R. Chambers, Christopher Croke, Yevgeny Liokumovich and Haomin Wen, “Area of convex disks”, arXiv:1701.06594 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06594

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “Although in all dimensions there are known (nonsharp) constants $C(n)$ such that $Vol(B(p,R))\geq C(n)(\frac {2R} \pi)^n$ (see for $n=2,3$ and for all $n$) even the two dimensional case of the conjecture is open: For a two dim”

title: The Prague-dimension upper-bound conjecture for random graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be sampled from the binomial random graph model ${\mathcal G}(n,p)$, where $p$ is a constant with $0<p<1$. Let $f_{\rm Pra}(G)$ denote the Prague dimension of $G$, namely the smallest number of vertex-distinguishing good colorings of $G$. **Prague-dimension conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_{2,\rm Pra}=c_{2,\rm Pra}(p)>0$ such that, with high probability as $n\to\infty$,

$$
f_{\rm Pra}(G)<c_{2,\rm Pra}\frac{n}{\log n}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the Prague dimension of a typical dense random graph is at most of order $n/\log n$. The paper notes that a matching lower bound follows from the corresponding lower bound for the Kneser rank and the inequality relating Kneser rank to Prague dimension; the conjectured upper bound remains open in the source.
source_name: Zoltán Füredi and Ida Kantor, “Kneser ranks of random graphs and minimum difference representations”, arXiv:1701.08292 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.08292

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: The clique-cover chromatic-index upper-bound conjecture for random graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be sampled from the binomial random graph model ${\mathcal G}(n,p)$, where $p$ is a constant with $0<p<1$. Let $\theta'_0(G)$ be the minimum, over all clique covers of $G$, of the chromatic index of the clique cover; equivalently, it is the smallest number of subgraphs with complete-graph components whose union covers $E(G)$. **Clique-cover chromatic-index conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_4=c_4(p)>0$ such that, with high probability as $n\to\infty$,

$$
\theta'_0(G)<c_4\frac{n}{\log n}.
$$

The conjecture proposes an $O(n/\log n)$ upper bound for the clique-cover chromatic index of a typical dense random graph. The source motivates it by suggesting that the Frieze--Reed method for random graph thickness may yield the correct order, but gives no proof.
source_name: Zoltán Füredi and Ida Kantor, “Kneser ranks of random graphs and minimum difference representations”, arXiv:1701.08292 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.08292

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

title: Maximum-gap sampling conjecture for shift-invariant spline spaces
statement:
Let $Q_m$ denote the spline generator and let $V(Q_m)$ be the shift-invariant spline space it generates. A sequence $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is **separated** if its distinct points have a positive minimum separation. **Maximum-gap sampling conjecture.** If $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is a separated set with

$$
\sup\limits_{i}(x_{i+\nu}-x_i)<\nu,
$$

then $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ is a stable set of sampling for $V(Q_m)$. This extends the known case $\nu=1$ and is motivated by the sharp maximum-gap results for entire functions of exponential type $\pi$ and the shift-invariant space generated by the Meyer scaling function; the corresponding assertion for general $\nu\geq 1$ remains open.
source_name: A. Antony Selvan, “A new sampling density condition for shift-invariant spaces”, arXiv:1702.00170 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00170

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: Maximum-gap derivative sampling conjecture for shift-invariant spaces
statement:
Let $V(\phi)$ be a shift-invariant space, let $k$ and $\nu$ be positive integers, and let $\\{x_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$ be a separated set. For a function $f$, consider the nonuniform samples of its derivatives $f^{(j)}(x_i)$ for $j=0,\dots,k-1$. **Maximum-gap derivative sampling conjecture.** If

$$
\sup\limits_{i}(x_{i+\nu}-x_i)<k\nu,
$$

then every function $f\in V(\phi)$ can be reconstructed stably from its nonuniform sample values $\\{f^{(j)}(x_i):j=0,\dots,k-1, i\in\mathbb{Z}\\}$. The statement generalizes the preceding maximum-gap sampling conjecture to simultaneous derivative sampling, but no resolution is given in the source.
source_name: A. Antony Selvan, “A new sampling density condition for shift-invariant spaces”, arXiv:1702.00170 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00170

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: Fomin–Zelevinsky's C-matrix conjecture for cluster algebras
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_{t_0}$ be the cluster algebra with principal coefficients at $\Sigma_{t_0}$, and let

$$
\Sigma_t=(X_t,\widetilde B_t)
$$

be a seed of $\mathcal A_{t_0}$ obtained from $\Sigma_{t_0}$ by iterated mutations. Write

$$
\widetilde B_t=\begin{pmatrix}B_t\\C_t\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $C_t$ is the lower part, called the **C-matrix**. **Fomin–Zelevinsky's C-matrix conjecture.** The seed $\Sigma_t$ is uniquely determined by $C_t$. This conjecture concerns the extent to which coefficient data determine seeds in cluster algebras; in the setting of the paper, the stated result is proved using positivity of cluster variables and sign-coherence of $c$-vectors, while related weaker conclusions are discussed for the sign-skew-symmetric case.
source_name: Peigen Cao, Min Huang and Fang Li, “A conjecture on C-matrices of cluster algebras”, arXiv:1702.01221 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01221

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The complete multipartite fractional-defect conjecture
statement:
For positive integers $m$, $a$, and $k$, let $K^{(m)}_a$ be the complete $m$-partite graph with $a$ vertices in each partite set. Let $D(G,k)$ denote the minimum defect in a fractional $k$-coloring of $G$. **Complete multipartite fractional-defect conjecture.** The minimum defect in a $k$-coloring of $K^{(m)}_a$ is

$$
\left(\left\lceil \frac{m}{k}\right\rceil-1\right)a.
$$

When $m$ is a multiple of $k$, this value is known to be optimal. The conjecture concerns the remaining values of $m$ and predicts that the natural upper bound remains exact.
source_name: Wayne Goddard and Honghai Xu, “Colorings with Fractional Defect”, arXiv:1702.01442 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: Kahn's bounded-degree spanning tree conjecture
statement:
Fix $\Delta$, and let $T=(T_n)$ be a fixed sequence of trees on $n$ vertices satisfying $\Delta(T)\le \Delta$. Write $G(n,p)$ for the binomial random graph.

**Kahn's conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that, if $p\ge C\log n/n$, then $G(n,p)$ almost surely contains $T$.

This conjecture asserts that the Hamilton-path threshold extends to every fixed sequence of spanning trees with bounded maximum degree. The source reports substantial partial results, including Montgomery's bound $p\ge \Delta\log^5 n/n$, and mentions announced work toward a proof, but does not mark the conjecture as resolved.
source_name: Julia Böttcher, “Large-scale structures in random graphs”, arXiv:1702.02648 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02648

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: The bounded-degree spanning graph threshold conjecture
statement:
Fix a constant $\Delta$, and let $H=(H_n)$ be a sequence of graphs with maximum degree $\Delta(H)\le \Delta$ and at most $n$ vertices, $v(H)\le n$.

**Bounded-degree spanning graph threshold conjecture.** The random graph $G(n,p)$ almost surely contains $H$ whenever

$$
p\cdot\frac{n^{2/(\Delta+1)}}{(\log n)^{1/\binom{\Delta+1}{2}}}\to\infty.
$$

Equivalently, the conjectured threshold is the threshold for a $K_{\Delta+1}$-factor. The source says this optimum is widely believed and gives no resolution.
source_name: Julia Böttcher, “Large-scale structures in random graphs”, arXiv:1702.02648 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02648

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: Resilience conjecture for universality of bounded-degree spanning trees
statement:
Fix $\Delta\ge 2$ and $\gamma>0$. Let $\mathcal{T}(n,\Delta)$ denote the family of spanning trees on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. The **local resilience** of a graph with respect to a property is the largest number of incident edges that may be deleted at every vertex while the property is retained.

**Bounded-degree tree universality resilience conjecture.** The conclusion of the cited resilience theorem—that the local resilience of $G(n,p)$ with respect to being universal for $\mathcal{T}(n,\Delta)$ is almost surely at least $\frac12-\gamma$—holds for $p\ge C\log n/n$.

The source says this probability is conjectured to be optimal up to constants, while the stated theorem only establishes the conclusion for $p\ge C(\log n/n)^{1/3}$.
source_name: Julia Böttcher, “Large-scale structures in random graphs”, arXiv:1702.02648 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02648

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: The spherical-twist conjecture for generic monodromy around discriminants
statement:
Let a component of the discriminant in the parameter space of a GLSM be given, and let the associated Higgs GLSM determine a category of D-branes, denoted by $\mathsf{A}$. A spherical twist is the autoequivalence associated with a spherical functor from $\mathsf{A}$ to the D-brane category of the original theory.

**Generic monodromy conjecture.** The generic monodromy around the component of the discriminant is given by a spherical twist, where $\mathsf{A}$ is the category of D-branes in the associated Higgs GLSM.

This conjecture identifies the category of massless D-branes in the Higgs GLSM as the source category governing generic monodromy. The surrounding discussion motivates the claim through spherical functors, but does not establish it in general; its status is therefore open.
source_name: Paul S. Aspinwall, M. Ronen Plesser and Kangkang Wang, “Mirror Symmetry and Discriminants”, arXiv:1702.04661 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.04661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: The bounded-degree decomposition conjecture for 4-edge-connected graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a $4$-edge-connected graph with maximum degree at most $5$. **The bounded-degree decomposition conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be decomposed into two connected factors $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that

$$
\Delta(G_2)\le 3.
$$

The source proposes this as the special case $m_1=m_2=1$ of a decomposition problem, and notes that it would improve a lower bound for connected factors at odd-degree vertices. No resolution is given.
source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “Modulo orientations with bounded out-degrees”, arXiv:1702.07039 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: Jaeger–Swart cyclic-connectivity conjecture for snarks
statement:
A **snark** is a bridgeless cubic class 2 graph satisfying the paper's snark definition. Its cyclic connectivity is the minimum size of an edge cut separating two subgraphs that each contain a cycle.

**Jaeger–Swart cyclic-connectivity conjecture.** If $G$ is a snark, then its cyclic connectivity is at most $6$.

The conjecture concerns the possible cyclic connectivity of snarks and is presented as an open general property of bridgeless cubic class 2 graphs. No resolution is given in the paper.
source_name: M. A. Fiol, G. Mazzuoccolo and E. Steffen, “On measures of edge-uncolorability of cubic graphs: A brief survey and some new results”, arXiv:1702.07156 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

title: The maximal-orbit conjecture for $C_{1,n}$
statement:
Let $m\ne n$, let $s$ be a finite sequence, and let $C_{m,n}(s,-)$ be the length-preserving bijection on finite sequences over $\{m,n\}$. For even $n>0$ and $j>0$, let

$$
t=1^{2j-1}.
$$

**Maximal-orbit conjecture for $C_{1,n}$.** The orbit of $t$ under the map $C_{1,n}(1,-)$ has length $2^j$. The general orbit bound proved in the source shows that this is the maximum possible length for sequences of length $2j-1$, and the equivalent odd-length formulation concerns $E_{1,n}\left(1^{2^j},1^{2j}\right)$.
source_name: Bobby Shen, “The Kolakoski sequence and related conjectures about orbits”, arXiv:1702.08156 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08156

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2017). “The Kolakoski sequence begins $1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, \ldots.$ There are many open problems associated with the Kolakoski sequence.”

title: Covert–Koh–Pham even-dimensional k-resultant modulus conjecture
statement:
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_k\subset\mathbb F_q^d$, with $k\geq 2$, and define

$$
\Delta_k(E_1,\ldots,E_k)=\left\{\left\|{\bf x}^1+\cdots+{\bf x}^k\right\|\in\mathbb F_q:{\bf x}^j\in E_j,\ j=1,\ldots,k\right\}.
$$

Let $\gamma_k$ be the smallest exponent such that $\prod_{j=1}^k|E_j|\geq Cq^{\gamma_k}$ implies $|\Delta_k(E_1,\ldots,E_k)|\geq cq$. **Covert–Koh–Pham conjecture.** If $d\geq 2$ is even and $k\geq 2$, then

$$
\gamma_k=\frac{kd}{2}.
$$

The exponent is motivated by the example $q=p^2$ with $E_j=\mathbb F_p^d$, which has product size $q^{kd/2}$ but a generalized resultant modulus set of size only $\sqrt q$. The problem remains open in the stated even-dimensional generality.
source_name: David Covert, Doowon Koh and Youngjin Pi, “The generalized k-resultant modulus set problem in finite fields”, arXiv:1703.00609 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00609

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2017).

title: The conjecture that scaled Segre varieties realize every ML degree up to their degree
statement: Let $V^c$ be the scaled Segre variety associated with an $m\times n$ scaling matrix $c\in(\mathbb C^*)^{mn}$, and let $\deg(V)=\binom{m+n-2}{m-1}$. **Scaled Segre ML-degree conjecture.** For each $i\in\{1,\ldots,\deg(V)\}$, there exists $c\in(\mathbb C^*)^{mn}$ such that $V^c$ has ML degree $i$. The examples in the source exhibit this phenomenon for the $3\times3$ case, while the general assertion is presented without a resolution.
source_name: Carlos Améndola, Nathan Bliss, Isaac Burke, Courtney R. Gibbons, Martin Helmer, Serkan Hoşten, Evan D. Nash, Jose Israel Rodriguez and Daniel Smolkin, “The Maximum Likelihood Degree of Toric Varieties”, arXiv:1703.02251 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).
